links.note: Literally, “From where these things to this man?”
Greek uses the single noun “homeland.”
Greek doubles the negation; English uses one “no.”
Repeating “two” means two at a time.
English adds “or” between the descriptions.
English makes the implied resurrection explicit.
Greek describes holding a grudge against him.
The compound participle means reclining together at table.
Greek describes those reclining at the meal.
The noun denotes a member of the royal guard.
Greek says to come apart privately.
Greek says the sheep “do not have” a shepherd.
Greek describes the hour as already far advanced.
Greek describes the hour as already far advanced.
The genitive of price expresses the bread’s cost.
Greek repeats “dining groups” distributively.
Greek repeats the noun to describe separate rows.
The dative means “to all”; English renders it “among them all.”
Greek “into” is rendered “up” for reaching the mountain.
Greek expresses his intention with “wanted.”
The verb means mooring the boat to shore.
The relative adverb marks the destination.
